checks.detail: PRNGKey(42) twice gives a bit-identical PSF (True); PRNGKey(1) does not (False). ops.shot_noise draws only from the key it is handed, so the whole retrieval is replayable.
checks.name: the_shot_noisy_forward_model_is_reproducible_given_a_key

checks.detail: upstream divides its wave-valued coefficients by 2*pi/lambda, so 5.0 waves becomes 0.423352 in the same length unit as the 0.532 um wavelength. zernike_aberrations(normalize=False) consumes that unit, not radians and not waves.
checks.name: the_coefficients_are_in_length_units_not_waves_or_radians

checks.detail: after 1000 steps of upstream's exact recipe (initial opt_state re-passed every iteration) the loss is 0.136827 against upstream's published 0.00174069, a factor of 79. Unlike c10_seidel_fitting, honouring the stale-optimizer-state detail does not rescue this one.
checks.name: upstreams_converged_loss_is_not_reproduced

checks.detail: mean squared coefficient error 1.710334e-02 against upstream's published 6.355736e-06: a different solution, not a noisier version of the same one.
checks.name: upstreams_coefficient_error_is_not_reproduced

checks.detail: 5.598808 -> 0.13682713, a 41x reduction over 1000 steps. The optimizer, the gradient path and the forward model all work; it is the solution that is wrong.
checks.name: the_loss_nevertheless_falls_by_more_than_an_order_of_magnitude

checks.detail: the running minimum of the loss never rises over 1000 steps
checks.name: the_loss_history_is_monotonically_non_increasing_in_its_running_minimum

checks.detail: all 10 coefficient gradients finite and non-zero at the first step: |grad| in [4.340e-03, 3.999e+00]. jax.grad flows through objective_point_source -> zernike_aberrations -> phase_change -> ff_lens -> intensity.
checks.name: every_coefficient_receives_a_finite_gradient

checks.detail: coefficients whose truth is 0 come back at [1.842, -0.945, -0.638, 2.315] waves, and the >= 2-wave terms at [0.047, 3.992, 1.464]. The two groups are not separated. c10_seidel_fitting DOES separate them, and the difference in the two examples' code is that c10 projects its coefficients onto the non-negative orthant after every step (eqx.tree_at(..., jnp.abs(...))) while this one does not -- which is what breaks the sign/twin ambiguity of single-intensity phase retrieval.
checks.name: the_fit_does_not_separate_present_from_absent_aberrations

checks.detail: upstream's loop passes the INITIAL opt_state on every iteration because its update() returns only (model, metrics). Rebinding the state -- the intended Adam pattern -- gives a final loss of 0.150986 and a mean squared coefficient error of 1.320843e-02, against 0.136827 and 1.710334e-02 for upstream's recipe. BOTH are far from the published 0.00174069 and 6.355736e-06. With the state frozen every step is a fresh bias-corrected Adam step, i.e. sign descent at a fixed step of lr, which escapes the local minimum accumulated moments settle into -- and in c10_seidel_fitting that IS what makes the published numbers reproduce. Here neither convention reaches them, so the missing ingredient is c10's non-negativity projection rather than the optimizer state.
checks.name: threading_the_adam_state_through_does_not_rescue_it_either

demonstrates: chromatix.functional.objective_point_source / phase_change / ff_lens, chromatix.utils.zernike_aberrations(ansi_indices, coefficients, normalize=False), chromatix.ops.shot_noise, and jax.grad through an equinox.Module forward model driven by optax.adam.
notes: Do NOT use this example as evidence that Chromatix phase retrieval converges; use c10_seidel_fitting for that. What this one establishes is narrower and still useful: jax.grad flows through objective_point_source -> zernike_aberrations -> phase_change -> ff_lens -> Field.intensity with finite non-zero gradients on all ten coefficients, ops.shot_noise is key-deterministic, and a NumPy array cannot be an eqx.field(static=True) if the module reaches jax.jit from more than one construction site.
title: Aberration Phase Retrieval (Zernike Fitting)
